summary: Mercury's 17-year mahadasha is described in every source as a period of learning, speech, trade, friends and family happiness, with honour from rulers or superiors when Mercury is strong. When Mercury is joined with malefics, debilitated, combust or in the 6th, 8th or 12th, the same period brings quarrels with relatives, losses, nervous or wind ailments and trouble from authorities. BPHS adds that the start is good, the middle brings recognition and the last part is troubled.
themes: wind and nervous ailments when afflicted
common_outcomes: gain of wealth, reputation and knowledge, royal favour, auspicious functions, happiness from wife and children, profit in business, when Mercury is well placed (BPHS 47.62-65)
meeting friends, personal comforts, fame through the praise of learned people, favour from elders, skill in speech, doing good to others, an elevated position (Phaladeepika 19.10)
money through seniors, relatives and friends, fame and happiness, going on an embassy or errand, income from dealing in gold, some wind ailment (Jataka Parijata 18.133)
garments, large wealth, grain, position, a mansion, fulfilment of wishes when Mercury is auspicious (Uttara Kalamrita, 'Dasas and their effects' sl. 8-9)
rare_outcomes: gain of new lands, cows and horses; money through Brahmins; worship of great men and gods; illness from wind, heat and phlegm (Phaladeepika 19.24, a second verse on Mercury's dasa)
journey to a foreign country and dependence on others when Mercury is with malefics (BPHS 47.66)
loss of wealth through lascivious habits, rheumatism and jaundice when Mercury is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68)
book writing and fame as a communicator when Mercury is linked to the houses of writing and fame (P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, example 52)

by_area.personality: Clear speech, cleverness and a helpful nature (Phaladeepika 19.10); growth of intelligence (BPHS 47.63). When Mercury is afflicted: short temper and weakened intellect (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.career: Favour from government and superiors, good standing, profit in trade (BPHS 47.62-65); an elevated position (Phaladeepika 19.10); errands or embassies (Jataka Parijata 18.133). Punishment or displeasure from government when Mercury is with malefics or in a dusthana (BPHS 47.66-68); trouble from the trading class (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.finance: Wealth through business, seniors, relatives and friends (BPHS 47.64; Jataka Parijata 18.133); dealing in gold (Jataka Parijata 18.133). Loss of wealth, land and cattle when Mercury is in the 6th, 8th or 12th (BPHS 47.67-68).
by_area.health: Good health when Mercury is strong (BPHS 47.64). Wind ailments (Jataka Parijata 18.133); wind, heat and phlegm disorders (Phaladeepika 19.24); urinary trouble when Mercury is with malefics; rheumatism and jaundice when in a dusthana (BPHS 47.66-68).
by_area.relationships: Happiness from wife and children (BPHS 47.64; Phaladeepika 19.10). Marriage is mentioned for Mercury in Aries, Gemini, Leo and Virgo (Raman, HPA pp. 264-265); loss of wife and children for Mercury in Scorpio (Raman).
by_area.family: Birth of children in the early part (BPHS 47.69); enmity with relatives when Mercury is with malefics (BPHS 47.66); loss of relations when Mercury is malefic (Uttara Kalamrita sl. 8-9).
by_area.spirituality: Worship of gods and great men, benefit from spiritual teachers (Phaladeepika 19.24); religious and charitable work for Mercury in Aries, Virgo and Sagittarius; recitation of scriptures for Gemini and Capricorn (Raman, HPA pp. 264-265).

strengtheners: Mercury exalted, in its own sign or a friendly sign (BPHS 47.62)
Mercury in the 5th, 9th or 11th (Santhanam's reading) or in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona (Sanskrit gloss) (BPHS 47.62)
aspect of a benefic, placement in the 9th, or Mercury ruling the 10th, which gives the good results in full (BPHS 47.65)
Mercury in an upachaya house from the lagna (Jataka Parijata 18.14, 18.16)
weakeners_or_cancellations: debilitation, an enemy's sign, or the 6th or 12th: a benefic then gives only untoward results (Phaladeepika 20.27)
combustion ('eclipsed' by the Sun): adverse results (Phaladeepika 20.14)
lagna_or_context_notes: Phaladeepika 20.50-51 says benefics that own kendras turn harmful, but Mercury does less harm as a kendra lord than Jupiter or Venus do. This matters for Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces lagnas, where Mercury rules two kendras. BPHS 47.65 names Mercury as lord of the 10th as a strengthening condition. Raman (HPA ch. XXIV, rules 3, 5, 10-11) says the dasa gives results by the houses Mercury rules, occupies and aspects, and that lords of the 6th and 8th give harm unless otherwise redeemed. P.V.R. Narasimha Rao (ch. 16.5.3, following Sanjay Rath) judges a mahadasha mainly from the Sun's position, so Mercury in the 2nd from the Sun, which forms Vesi yoga, gives that yoga's results in its dasa.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.61-70, tr. R. Santhanam vol. 2, pp. 585-586
source_views.view: Mercury exalted, in its own or a friendly sign, or in the 11th, 5th or 9th: wealth, reputation, knowledge, government favour, auspicious functions, happiness from wife and children, health, sweet food, business profits. Aspected by a benefic, in the 9th, or lord of the 10th: these results in full. With a malefic: punishment by government, enmity with kin, foreign travel, dependence on others, urinary trouble. In the 6th, 8th or 12th: losses through lust, rheumatism, jaundice, theft, government hostility, loss of land and cattle. The start brings wealth, education, children and happiness; the middle, recognition from government; the last part is distressing.

source_views.source: BPHS 47.61-70, Sanskrit with English gloss, enjoylearningsanskrit.com
source_views.view: Verse 62 asks for Mercury exalted, in its own or a friendly sign and also in a kendra, the 11th or a trikona. Verse 66 counts conjunction or aspect by malefics: royal displeasure, mental distress, conflict with kin, foreign travel. Verse 67 for the 6th, 8th or 12th: dependence, quarrels, fear of illness, loss of wealth. Verse 70: honour from the ruler in the middle, suffering at the end.

19.10: friends, comforts, fame from the learned, favour of elders, clever speech, helping others, happiness to family, a high position. 19.24: help from spiritual teachers, money through Brahmins, new lands, cows and horses, worship of the great and of gods, great wealth, but also wind, heat and phlegm diseases.

General rules that apply to Mercury: retrograde planets and those in own, exalted or friendly signs give the good results, while eclipsed (combust), debilitated, inimical or 6/8/12 planets give adverse ones (20.14); a vargottama planet gives good results (20.22); a benefic debilitated, in an enemy's sign or in the 6th or 12th gives only untoward results (20.27); Mercury as a kendra lord does less harm than Jupiter or Venus (20.51).

source_views.source: Jataka Parijata 18.133, with 18.14 and 18.16 (tr. V. Subrahmanya Sastri, vol. II)
source_views.view: 18.133: money through seniors, relatives and friends; fame and happiness; going on an embassy; income from gold; wind ailments. General rules: a dasa lord in an upachaya from the lagna, or in its own, exalted or friendly sign, or aspected by a benefic or friend, gives a good dasa (18.14, 18.16); the dasa is happy when the Moon's sign is the dasa lord's exaltation sign or a friendly sign, or is an upachaya, trikona or the 7th from the dasa lord (18.14).

source_views.source: Uttara Kalamrita, 'The Dasas and their effects', sl. 8-9 (tr. S.S. Sareen)
source_views.view: Auspicious Mercury: garments, great wealth, grain, position, prosperity, a mansion, relatives, success, wishes fulfilled. Malefic Mercury: going abroad, short temper, loss of relations, weakened intellect, trouble from traders, disputes, loss of land and money.

source_views.source: B.V. Raman, Hindu Predictive Astrology ch. XXIV, pp. 230-233 and 263-266
source_views.view: Results of Mercury's dasa by sign. Aries: marriage, religious and social work, charity, favour of rulers, gains from land and cattle. Taurus: great happiness, titles, authority, music. Gemini: great learning, completion of studies, fame, wealth, marriage. Cancer: disgrace, change of residence, fines or confinement, loss of land, enmity. Leo: courage, travel in hills, wealth from abroad, marriage, fame. Virgo: the best period of life, royal favour, health, unexpected gains. Libra: works published in one's name, favour of the wealthy and educated, leadership. Scorpio: loss of wife, children and riches, mental trouble, business losses, loss of reputation. Sagittarius: success in education, learned company, travel east. Capricorn: success in trade, new business, patronage, victory over foes. Aquarius: wealth, pleasure, good name. Pisces: theft, dysentery, litigation, quarrels with relatives, nervous breakdown, failure. General rules: the dasa lord gives results by ownership, association, placement and aspect, modified by navamsa and transits, and is never to be read verbatim.

source_views.source: P.V.R. Narasimha Rao, Vedic Astrology: An Integrated Approach, ch. 16.5-16.6 (examples 52, 54)
source_views.view: A planet gives in its dasa what its placements in the divisional charts promise. Rath's 'tripod' rule: judge the mahadasha from the Sun, the antardasha from the Moon. Examples: a Mercury dasa that brought book writing, with Mercury as significator of writing linked to the arudha of the 3rd and forming Vesi yoga from the Sun; a Mercury dasa in which the native became a chief minister, with Mercury well placed from the Sun and the Moon.

source_views.source: David Frawley, Astrology of the Seers, ch. 6 (planetary periods) pp. 202-203, and example charts pp. 284-285 (a novelist) and 308-309 (Roosevelt)
source_views.view: The major lord gives the results of the houses it rules and aspects. Examples: a Mercury period that brought out a writer's best work; a Mercury period of steadily rising political power, because Mercury as dispositor of a strong Mars carried Mars's power to the ascendant. Remedies at the start of a period: strengthen a weak benefic lord with its gem, propitiate a malefic one with mantra or worship.

source_views.source: Sanjay Rath, Crux of Vedic Astrology: Timing of Events (1998), pp. 389-390, 456-458
source_views.view: Examples only. An exalted Mercury in the 6th from the arudha lagna led gradually to renunciation, which came at the start of the Mercury dasa (sannyasa in Mercury-Venus). In Akbar's chart the Mercury dasa saw the founding of a synthetic faith, with Moon and Mercury in close aspect.

disagreements: BPHS 47.62: Santhanam lists the 11th, 5th or 9th as an alternative to good dignity, while the Sanskrit gloss requires good dignity and also a kendra, the 11th or a trikona. BPHS gives the end of the dasa as distressing; Phaladeepika and Jataka Parijata do not divide the period. Phaladeepika 19.10 is wholly favourable, while 19.24 adds wind, heat and phlegm diseases. Raman makes Cancer, Scorpio and Pisces bad signs for this dasa even though Pisces is only Mercury's debilitation sign and Cancer and Scorpio are not named by the classical dasa verses. Phaladeepika 20.14 treats retrogression as favourable; other sources here are silent.
phrasing_guidance: Frame this as a long period for study, communication, trade and networks, whose tone depends on Mercury's dignity, house and associations. Mention the troubled version only when the chart shows the listed conditions, and keep health notes general (nerves, digestion), with no diagnosis. Present the BPHS start-middle-end pattern as a tendency, not a certainty.

remedies.remedy: if Mercury is benefic but weak, strengthen it with its gem at the start of the period; if it acts as a malefic, propitiate it with mantra, ritual or worship (general rule, not Mercury-specific)
remedies.source: Frawley, Astrology of the Seers p. 203

phases: BPHS 47.69-70: the start brings wealth, progress in education, birth of children and happiness; the middle brings recognition from government; the last part is distressing. Phaladeepika 20.57: a combust or debilitated Mercury in an auspicious sign or navamsa gives its good effects in the later part. Frawley (p. 203): the opening sub-period of a benefic's dasa plants seeds rather than fruit, and is a good time to set goals.
